what_it_does: splits a BeautifulSoup page into (id, header, text) sections by converting it to markdown and walking its lines

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `text` is rebuilt as `text + "\n" + line` for every line of a section; collecting lines in a list and joining at the flush points (91-93, 99) writes each line once. The string is local, but `text = text + ...` is not the in-place `+=` form, so CPython copies the buffer each time

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: markdownify(str(soup)) re-parses the HTML, and the reparse normalises the markup; calling convert_soup directly was not shown to give identical markdown, so behaviour preservation cannot be claimed

what_it_does: escapes XML inside Jekyll highlight-xml blocks of an HTML string

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: a single re.sub would change behaviour when a block's text also occurs outside a highlight block (str.replace rewrites every occurrence); the exact-preserving edit (skip when escaped == match) saves almost nothing on XML blocks, which nearly always contain < or >

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: re caches compiled patterns, so the string pattern costs one dictionary lookup per call; no measurable work to remove

what_it_does: picks a code-block language from a Jekyll highlight tag or by sniffing for curl / import com.yahoo

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `el.text` is BeautifulSoup get_text(), which walks the element's descendants and joins strings; it is evaluated up to three times per code block on the same unchanged element, once is enough

what_it_does: reads a doc JSON, splits each HTML page into paragraph documents, merges question expansions and writes paragraph_index.json

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: re.sub with a string pattern hits re's compiled-pattern cache; hoisting would save a dictionary lookup per call, not a mechanism worth an edit, and main reads sys.argv and writes a fixed file so it cannot be measured cleanly

what_it_does: sums per-document term counts into corpus counts and counts how many documents contain each term

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: for every term in `terms` it iterates all documents and builds a list of 0/1 flags, O(terms x docs) dictionary probes; each per-document dict holds a term once, so incrementing a `docs` counter in the summing loop at 93-97 gives the same number in one pass

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `total_count` is summed per document and never read; deleting the line removes a pass over every document's values

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: the list of per-document dicts is needed by the summing loop; without the quadratic scan it could be a generator but that only saves memory, not work

what_it_does: counts n-grams of up to term_length words in a tokenised document, skipping windows containing a common word

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: for every window it slices the list, builds a lambda and map and runs any() over win_len words, then slices again for the join; testing each word once into a flags list and prefix sum turns the common-word test into two index reads per window and only valid windows are sliced

what_it_does: counts terms in title and content and returns their summed counts

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the comprehension iterates list(title_counts.keys()) + list(content_counts.keys()), allocating two lists and a concatenation, and calls .get twice per key; copying title_counts and adding content counts touches each key once. Key order (title keys first, then new content keys) is preserved

what_it_does: builds update operations for each term and dumps them as indented JSON

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `re.sub(r" ", "/", term)` enters the regex engine per term; str.replace gives the same string without it

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: dropping indent=2 changes the bytes of the output file, which is part of the contract

what_it_does: deletes every character whose Unicode category starts with C from a string

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: calls unicodedata.category once per character inside a Python generator over all text; a str.translate table that fills itself via __missing__ calls category once per distinct code point and translates in C

what_it_does: builds per-impression tensors for impressions that have both clicked and skipped items

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the three index lists and user_index are built for every impression before the `sum(labels) > 0 and sum(labels) != len(labels)` test; impressions failing it (all clicked or none clicked) are discarded after the work is done. Testing first skips that work

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: caching the tensors per prob/train changes object identity and state the callers could mutate, and random.random() must still be consumed to keep the RNG stream the same

what_it_does: appends user, news, category, subcategory and entity indices for each positive and its sampled negatives

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: each sampled row does three separate self.news_content[idx][key] lookups, i.e. three attribute loads and three dict lookups on the same entry; one lookup serves all three

what_it_does: parses impression rows into dicts of user index, timestamp, news indices and labels

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the parsed datetime is stored in impression_list under "timestamp", which is part of the unit's effect on its argument; removing the parse changes it

what_it_does: returns the relevance of each requested news id from a Vespa result

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: find_hit scans all hits for every id, O(ids x hits); building a dict from news_id to first hit once makes each lookup constant time. A missing id still gives None and a TypeError at hit["relevance"], as before

what_it_does: linear search for a news id in a result's children

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the repair is the dict in predictions, its only caller (grep); changing find_hit alone cannot remove the repeated scan

what_it_does: writes one tab-separated line per id with the embedding formatted to six decimals

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `embeddings[index]` creates a tensor view and .tolist() a list per id, hundreds of thousands of times; one embeddings.tolist() converts the matrix in one call and rows are indexed as lists

what_it_does: computes user and news embeddings from the model and writes them as TSV

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: both embedding calls record an autograd graph through embeddings, linear layers and sigmoid although the result is only written; under torch.no_grad() no graph is built. Written values are identical

what_it_does: trains the model for `epochs` epochs, evaluating and saving embeddings after each

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: save_embeddings runs a full forward pass and rewrites both files every epoch, each overwriting the last; running it once after the loop (guarded by epochs > 0) leaves the same final files

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: eval_model prints metrics; removing or thinning the call changes printed output

what_it_does: one epoch of mini-batch training that prints the summed loss

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the printed total_loss is a tensor with grad_fn in the output text; accumulating loss.item() would change the printed output

what_it_does: writes a tab then the embedding as comma-separated %.4f

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: about 1000 f.write calls per document (value and comma separately); one write of a joined string does the same bytes with one call

what_it_does: runs BERT over each document and writes the [CLS] vector

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the forward pass builds an autograd graph (no torch.no_grad) and outputs[0].tolist() converts the whole 1 x tokens x 512 tensor to nested lists to keep row 0; a no_grad block and outputs[0][0, 0].tolist() give the same numbers with less work. Batching was left out because it changes padding and floating-point results

what_it_does: writes one JSON put-operation per unseen news row, joined by commas

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: json.dump(doc, output) goes through json's pure-Python iterencode and issues one write per token; output.write(json.dumps(doc)) uses the C one-shot encoder and one write, identical bytes

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: csv.reader with positional access would raise IndexError on short rows where DictReader fills None, so it does not preserve behaviour on all inputs

what_it_does: random day in November 2019 as an int yyyymmdd

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: fromtimestamp uses local time zone, so a precomputed table would not preserve behaviour across zones, and the saving per call is small

what_it_does: writes user embeddings as a Vespa feed JSON array

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `"%.6f" % v` is applied to numpy float32 scalars, which are converted through numpy's scalar machinery per element; embedding.tolist() yields Python floats with the same value, so the formatted text is identical

what_it_does: writes news embeddings as a Vespa feed update array

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: same per-element numpy scalar formatting as in convert_user_embeddings; the same edit with tolist() applies

what_it_does: applies each Liquid-transform regex substitution to a command string

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: every transform pattern starts with a literal '{', yet each re.sub scans the whole command; a command without '{' cannot match any, so returning early skips all the scans

what_it_does: parses an HTML page into before/steps/after script lists from data-test attributes

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: a Python lambda is called for every tag in the document; find_all(["pre","div","p"], attrs={"data-test": True}) filters inside bs4's matcher in document order and calls the Python-level callback for none

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: re.search/re.sub with literal patterns hit the re cache; the work removed is a lookup, and it runs only on tags that have data-test

what_it_does: joins a <pre> element's child nodes into file content

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `content +=` on a local str is resized in place by CPython, so the concatenation is not quadratic here

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `str(type(line))` builds a string such as "<class 'bs4.element.NavigableString'>" for every child node only to test a substring; testing type(line).__name__ avoids the string build with the same truth value, since the module path contains no 'ProcessingInstruction'

what_it_does: fetches or reads pages and runs them

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the number of pages is small and each page costs a network or disk read; copying bytes is negligible next to it, and the unit starts docker commands so cannot be measured

what_it_does: appends output to a log and echoes it when verbose and not filtered

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: re.match(None, s) raises TypeError when no filter has been set; testing _verbose first would stop raising, which changes the exception behaviour

what_it_does: loads each page image, then yields a blended base64 heatmap per image and unfiltered query token

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: img_pil.copy() duplicates every full page image and processed_images keeps a second list of them that is never read; _blend_image only uses original_size, so the copy and the list are dead work

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: should_filter_token (a regex match) is evaluated for every image x token although the answer depends only on the token; computing the kept tokens once before the image loop removes (images-1) x tokens matches

what_it_does: fills a (maps, tokens, patches, patches) tensor from Vespa cell lists

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: hasattr and attribute read for image_seq_length run once per cell inside the innermost loop, thousands of times per call; the value is constant for the call

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: a vectorised index_put with duplicate addresses does not guarantee the last write wins, so equivalence with the sequential loop is not assured

what_it_does: True if a token matches the filter regex

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: re.compile with a literal is served from re's cache; the only hoist available lives outside the function source, and the saving is one cache lookup

what_it_does: waits for page images, generates similarity-map PNGs and writes them to disk

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: all([os.path.exists(p) for p in img_paths]) builds the full list so cannot stop at the first missing file and is evaluated again after the loop; any/all over a generator short-circuits and the final check can reuse the loop's last result

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: gen_similarity_maps PNG-encodes and base64-encodes each map and this loop immediately decodes it; yielding the PNG bytes from _blend_image and writing them removes an encode/decode pair per map (sole consumers: grep shows gen_similarity_maps is called only here and _blend_image only from gen_similarity_maps)

what_it_does: waits for page images then streams a Gemini answer as SSE messages

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `response_text = replace_newline_with_br(response_text)` rescans the whole accumulated answer for each chunk, O(n^2) in the answer length; replacing only the new chunk gives the same text because the earlier part is already newline-free

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: every retry pass restarts `images = []` and re-opens every ready file; keeping already opened images and only probing missing ones removes the repeated PIL opens

what_it_does: packs each float query vector into signed-byte bit vectors

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: np.where(cond, 1, 0) materialises an int64 array before packbits; packbits takes the boolean array directly and gives the same bits

what_it_does: packs each patch float vector into signed-byte bit vectors for the feed

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: same np.where int64 intermediate per patch (about 1030 per page); packbits on the boolean mask gives the same bytes

what_it_does: writes each document's cleaned text and its output byte offset

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: out.tell() on a text-mode file flushes the encoder and reconstructs a position every call; keeping a running byte count (encoded length of each string written) gives the same offsets and leaves the buffer to flush normally

what_it_does: reads one document at an offset, cleans title and body with regexes

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: patterns are literals served from re's cache; no mechanism beyond a lookup per call

what_it_does: reads all training queries and normalises each

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: dropping or deferring normalisation changes the returned dict, which is the unit's return value

what_it_does: True if a string is length-out-of-range or contains any filter substring

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: a Python-level loop over 30 keys does one `in` per iteration; any(map(text.__contains__, filters)) runs the loop in C with identical truth value and short-circuit

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `text.startswith("/") and len(text) < 3` is unreachable because line 58 already returned for len < 3; deleting it removes a startswith call per title and noun chunk

what_it_does: True if the text starts with any invalid prefix

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: a Python loop calling startswith per prefix; any(map(text.startswith, invalid_starts)) iterates in C, same result

what_it_does: queries Vespa for each unprocessed query and appends feature rows to a CSV

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `int(qid) not in processed_queries` scans a list for every query; a set built once from the list gives O(1) membership, while len() for the printed count still uses the list

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: replacing DataFrame.to_csv with the csv module could change float formatting in the file

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: moving the processed-queries write inside the if changes the contents of the processed file, a behaviour change (and a possible bug, not an energy repair)

what_it_does: reads the processed query ids as ints into a list

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the list-to-set repair belongs to build_dataset, which also needs len() with duplicates; readlines() copy alone is trivial

what_it_does: loads documents and queries from JSONL into dicts

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: file.readlines() materialises every line in a list before parsing; iterating the file object parses line by line without the list

what_it_does: returns an InputExample for a query with rotating positive and negative document

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: pop(0)+append rotates short lists; the lists are per-query positives/negatives of modest size and any cheaper structure changes the state shape other readers (none found) rely on

what_it_does: recall at count allowing ties in the ground-truth distances

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Python loop over numpy scalar subtractions and abs to find the end of the tie run; one vectorised comparison over true_dists[count:] finds the first non-tie index in one call

what_it_does: reads system_prompt.txt and returns its text

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: opens and reads the same static file on every chat request; a cached copy removes the open, read and decode per request (file is a packaged resource beside app.py)

what_it_does: writes product documents to JSONL

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: in --full mode iterrows builds a pandas Series (copying a row across all columns) for each of about 50k products; itertuples builds a namedtuple without the Series construction

what_it_does: aggregates order rows into user profile documents

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: iterrows builds a Series per purchase row for every user's purchases (about 1.4M rows in --full); building the list of dicts from column arrays removes the Series construction

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Counter would change the key order of user_profile in the JSON output

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: when not --full only the first `limit` users are written, but the merge covers all 1.4M train rows; restricting orders to the first `limit` user ids (isin on the train order ids) and the train rows to those orders before the merge writes the same users

what_it_does: aggregates order products into per-order arrays and writes order JSONL

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: agg with a Python lambda calls list() once per group through pandas' Python-function path; agg(list) / apply(list) gives the same lists with less per-group overhead

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: iterrows builds a Series per order row; itertuples avoids the Series construction

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: orders.csv is read again, but the first read is in process_users, a different unit; removing it needs main to pass the frame, which spreads the edit over callers

what_it_does: cross-validates a LightGBM model, then trains and exports the final model

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: removing lgb_train from valid_sets drops the logged training metrics, which changes log records

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: serialises the model dict to a string, runs one re.sub over the whole string per feature, and parses it back; renaming the entries in feature_names, feature_infos and feature_importances directly avoids F full-string scans

what_it_does: embeds each sampled frame of a video with CLIP

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: batching frames changes floating-point results of CLIP, and the loop-invariant basename/split work is negligible next to a CLIP forward pass

what_it_does: samples equally spaced frames from a list

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: np.array(images) stacks every frame (a copy of all pixel data) before the few sampled ones are indexed; selecting from the list first stacks only the sampled frames

what_it_does: turns condition strings into Vespa query-builder conditions

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: creating seven small lambdas per call is negligible next to the query-builder calls that follow; the only hoist is outside the function
